subject: Proposed Diversity Director and Human Resources Merger
overview: The Council rejected a mayoral proposal to merge the diversity director role into human resources, voting instead to maintain a standalone position. Members also approved a comprehensive plan to address city road and sidewalk conditions and authorized a $500,000 water rate subsidy.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Condolences
items.summary: Approved resolutions honoring Ben Ercolini's retirement, the late Melissa Menounos, and officer Harold McGillivray Jr., whose name was added to the National Law Enforcement Memorial. The meeting was dedicated to the memory of Harold McGillivray Jr.

items.title: Contract Negotiation Update Request
items.summary: Approved a request for the administration to provide an update on the status of contract negotiations with Building and Recreation Department staff.

items.title: Road Infrastructure and Capital Planning
items.summary: Approved a request for a comprehensive road repaving plan and infrastructure spending report, amended to include a city-wide count of tree stumps and a pilot program for recycled asphalt. Councilors discussed using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds for these capital needs.

items.title: COVID-19 Update
items.summary: Public Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor reported that case counts reached single digits and discussed upcoming vaccination clinics for ages 12 and older. Discussion included the hiring of a COVID-19 communications specialist and shifting state guidelines for sports and masks.

items.title: Personnel Ordinance Amendments
items.summary: Approved adding the Director of Economic Development to the classification plan but rejected a proposal to merge the Diversity Director and Human Resources roles. Councilors argued that maintaining a standalone diversity official is essential for the city's equity goals.

items.title: Water and Sewer Retained Earnings Appropriation
items.summary: Approved appropriating $500,000 from retained earnings to subsidize the fiscal year 2022 water and sewer budget and limit the rate increase to 3%. The Council discussed the need for future water meter replacements to ensure accurate billing.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents addressed the Council regarding free speech protections following comments at a Human Rights Commission meeting and the need for evidence-based reading instruction for students with dyslexia. A resident also reported a missed trash collection on Riverside Avenue, which the clerk was directed to communicate to the administration.
